title: Paluck Technologies Ltd - 544897 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Analyst / Investor Meet - Outcome

summary.headline: Paluck Technologies guides FY27 revenue of INR130-140 crores and PAT of INR17-18 crores, about 25% growth, with H1 PAT of about INR5 crores.
summary.overview: Management said H1 FY27 growth was organic, with revenue up about 34% and PAT up about 40-42%, to roughly INR51.2 crores of revenue and about INR5 crores of PAT. Full-year FY27 guidance is INR130-140 crores of revenue and INR17-18 crores of PAT, implying a heavy H2 (about 60% of revenue). Management said IPO proceeds were not yet deployed in H1 and expects their impact in FY28, with FY28 revenue targeted at INR190-200 crores. On the call, operating cash flow was negative (about negative INR9 crores), trade receivables rose about 80% YoY, and H1 operating margin was about 17%, which management attributed to timing and one-off items.

financial_highlights.value: INR51.2 crores (telecom/auto & engineering services INR27.15 crores; equipment rental INR24 crores)
About negative INR9 crores (as cited by analyst)

financial_highlights.change: Below 20-23% in H1 FY26 and H2 FY26
Up about 80% YoY (as cited by analyst)

financial_highlights.value: About INR4.5-5 crores, down from about INR50 crores over 3-4 years

segments.name: Telecom / automobile & engineering services
segments.commentary: Manages about 60,000 telecom sites/nodes on O&M and managed-services contracts with 4-5 year terms; H1 FY27 revenue about INR27.15 crores (+38% YoY); gross margin about 20-23%. Revenue split was about 49% of FY26 revenue (INR56 crores).

segments.name: Construction equipment rental
segments.commentary: Fleet of about 190-192 machines rented to Tata Projects, L&T, Megha, HCC, Shivalaya, NKC and Patel; H1 FY27 revenue about INR24 crores (+29% YoY); gross margin about 35%; contracts of 3-5 years. FY26 revenue about INR55 crores (about 51% share).

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue guidance of INR130-140 crores (about 25% growth), implying H2 revenue of about INR85-90 crores.
FY27 PAT guidance of INR17-18 crores (about 25% growth), implying H2 PAT of about INR12-13 crores.
FY28 revenue targeted at about INR190-200 crores, with about 40% growth from FY28 onwards once IPO proceeds are deployed; organic growth about 25%.
Expects about INR50 crores of recurring orders to materialise within 2-3 months.
Five-year target of about 4x growth, subject to meeting capital requirements.
Management said guidance is conservative. Operating margin for the full year is expected to match the prior year despite lower H1 margin.
capex_capacity: IPO funds were not utilised in H1 FY27; utilisation expected in H2 FY27 and FY28, mainly for capex on construction equipment and telecom inventory.
Equipment rental is capex-heavy, requiring new machines every few years; telecom is working-capital-heavy because inventory must be held at sites nationwide.
Management said IPO-funded capex will lead to higher cash outflows in H2 FY27.
Current fleet is about 190-192 machines; no fleet expansion numbers were given.
demand_pricing: About 85-90% of business is recurring, with customer retention above 90%; management cited 7-8% annual inflation-linked growth on the recurring base.
Customers include Ericsson, Nokia, ZTE, Huawei, Airtel, Vodafone Idea and Reliance (telecom), and Tata Projects, L&T, Megha, HCC, Shivalaya, NKC and Patel (equipment).
Management cited high entry barriers in telecom (99.999% uptime requirements) and equipment rental (cement curing windows of 3-4 hours) and relationships of more than 10 years.
Seasonality: H1 is lighter (about 40% of revenue) due to the rainy season; H2 is about 60%.
Telecom sites are split about 55% South India and 45% North India; no pricing or competitive data given.

qa_highlights.question: What are the segment-wise gross margins, and what is the seasonality?
qa_highlights.answer: Telecom gross margin is about 20-23% and equipment leasing about 35%, with a blended 23-25%. H1 revenue is about 40% and H2 about 60% due to the rainy season, but PAT skews more to H2 (about one-third in H1, two-thirds in H2).

qa_highlights.question: Does FY27 guidance of INR139 crores revenue and INR18 crores PAT imply H2 of about INR88 crores revenue and INR13 crores PAT?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said H2 revenue would be about INR85-90 crores and H2 PAT about INR12-13 crores, giving full-year PAT of INR17-18 crores and revenue of INR130-140 crores.

qa_highlights.question: Why did H1 operating margin fall to about 17%, and will H2 margin recover?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said H1 had a higher recurrence of certain expenses, and that full-year margins will stay in line with the prior year.

qa_highlights.question: Why was H1 operating cash flow negative, and will it stay negative in H2?
qa_highlights.answer: Telecom inventory was replenished in H1, leading to working capital absorption of about INR10 crores. Management expects H2 operating cash flow to remain negative, with inventory days easing next year as scale grows; IPO capex will add outflows.

qa_highlights.question: Why did trade receivables rise about 80% YoY, and what is the ageing?
qa_highlights.answer: Normal ageing is 90-120 days with large corporate customers. Management attributed the rise to one-off delayed payments and expects receivables to decline in H2 in days terms.

qa_highlights.question: What is the earnings potential of the new capex, and what are FY28 revenue and margins?
qa_highlights.answer: Management targets FY28 revenue of INR190-200 crores, based on about INR50 crores of additional orders expected in 2-3 months. No margin figures for new capex were given.

risks_watch: H1 operating margin of about 17% vs 20-23% previously; management says full-year margin will hold.
Negative operating cash flow in H1 and expected in H2; working capital and IPO-funded capex raise funding needs.
Trade receivables up about 80% YoY; watch whether they fall in H2 as management expects.
Dependence on conversion of about INR50 crores of expected orders within 2-3 months to support FY28 revenue of INR190-200 crores.
Concentration in a small set of large customers and telecom operators; the company reports about 60,000 sites and a fleet of about 190 machines.
Management's FY28 growth claim (about 40%) and five-year 4x target depend on capital deployment, with no detailed capex figure or timeline given.
summary.management_tone: Confident and growth-focused on recurring revenue and FY27/FY28 targets, which management called conservative. Less clear on H1 margin decline, negative operating cash flow and the receivables build-up, which it attributed to timing and one-offs. Answers on capex quantum and new-asset returns were thin.
key_quotes: And all this organic growth that we have done in the first half has been done with organic growth because all the funds of the IPO came in September.
We have given a very conservative guidance and we are very hopeful of achieving the same.
Going forward, I think our receivables will reduce in H2 or so.

adds.what: IPO-funded capex on construction equipment (machines) and telecom inventory; no fleet expansion numbers given

growth.why: FY27 revenue guided to INR130-140 crores (~25% growth) and PAT INR17-18 crores, requiring H2 revenue of ~INR85-90 crores versus H1 INR51.2 crores; backing is partial, with ~INR50 crores of recurring orders expected in 2-3 months and IPO-funded capex (no fleet numbers) only lifting FY28 revenue to INR190-200 crores.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: H1 operating margin fell to about 17% vs 20-23% in H1 and H2 FY26, but management says full-year margin will match the prior year, implying H2 recovery is needed and not yet evidenced.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: IPO funds are expected to be used in H2 FY27 and FY28 for construction equipment and telecom inventory, with no fleet numbers given and FY28 revenue targeted at INR190-200 crores versus about INR130-140 crores in FY27.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: FY27 revenue guided to INR130-140 crores (about 25% growth), needing H2 revenue of about INR85-90 crores vs H1 INR51.2 crores, with about 85-90% recurring business and about INR50 crores of orders expected in 2-3 months.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Fleet of about 190-192 machines needs periodic replacement and IPO funds are slated for equipment purchases in H2 FY27 and FY28, though no capex quantum was given.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management called FY27 guidance conservative, but it is tied to a large H2 step-up (about 60% of revenue) and conversion of about INR50 crores of orders.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: H1 margin of about 17%, negative operating cash flow (about negative INR9 crores), receivables up about 80% YoY and reliance on a heavy H2 leave the INR130-140 crore target exposed to slippage.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: No new products, brands or models were discussed.

rows.label: About INR50 crores of recurring orders within 2-3 months
rows.why: Management expects about INR50 crores of recurring orders to materialise within 2-3 months, which it links to FY28 revenue of INR190-200 crores.

rows.label: Receivables and inventory normalisation
rows.why: Management expects receivables (up about 80% YoY, 90-120 day ageing) and inventory days to ease in H2 and next year, but H2 operating cash flow is still expected to be negative.

rows.label: Debt at about INR4.5-5 crores after cut from about INR50 crores
rows.why: Debt has already fallen from about INR50 crores over 3-4 years, but IPO-funded capex and negative cash flow point to more borrowing needs.

tone.note: Management was confident on recurring revenue and FY27/FY28 targets, calling them conservative, but was thin on the H1 margin drop, negative operating cash flow, receivables build-up and capex quantum, which analysts pushed on.
